newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac tells Euro parliament not to meddle.
newsitem.headline: Chirac tells Euro parliament not to meddle.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac denounced on Tuesday what he called unacceptable interference by the European Parliament in French internal affairs over a disputed immigration bill, his office said.

A spokesman said Chirac gave the parliament's new Spanish speaker Jose-Maria Gil-Robles a letter protesting after it narrowly adopted a resolution urging the government to drop the bill, clamping down on illegal immigration, and deploring the rise of the extreme-right in France.

The letter is "very firm" and denounces "interference in France's internal affairs", the spokesman said, adding that Chirac had also verbally expressed his concern that the assembly's stand last week was "unacceptable" because the parliament was not competent on immigration.
Earlier, Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told a regular briefing: "This matter is in no way in the field of competence of the European Parliament."

French National Assembly speaker Philippe Seguin took the same line in a luncheon toast for Gil-Robles, saying national parliaments should have a greater say in vetting European Union legislation and ensuring the principle of subsidiarity was respected.

"I am sure this wish will not shock your colleagues...except for those who cannot resist interfering in the internal affairs of France and even in matters currently under way in our assembly," he said in a clear reference to the immigration bill.
Seguin said the French government had been fulfilling its European obligations by proposing the legislation, designed to close loopholes in immigration law.

Whatever people thought of the bill, it was important that the respective rights of the national and European parliaments be clarified "to get out of the current shambles which leads only to a noisy and chaotic impotence".
